title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Chip Wipeout Closes a Rough October
conditions.summary: Tech got pounded as Intel and Reddit each lost about 29 percent and AI-spending worries spread, sending the Nasdaq down nearly 3 percent. Treasuries rallied, oil firmed on Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks, and gold and bitcoin slid.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The S&P 500 fell 1.83% to 7,578.97 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.84% to 25,442.31, its worst day since early June.
The Dow lost 1.06% to 51,785.82 and the Russell 2000 slid 2.03% to 2,801.16.
Earnings from Intel, Amazon and Reddit revived worries about Big Tech's heavy AI spending, and the selling deepened through the afternoon before a small late bounce off the lows.
Technology was the worst sector, down nearly 5%, with chip stocks hit hardest; energy held up as Exxon and Chevron touched record highs.
Breadth was weak, with nearly 70% of US stocks falling. For October, the Nasdaq lost about 5%, the S&P 500 about 1% and the Dow gained 1.5%.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: The third-quarter Employment Cost Index rose 0.8%, keeping wage pressure in view.
St. Louis Fed President Musalem and Richmond Fed President Barkin both said rates may need to go higher, after Thursday's hot September PCE inflation reading of 3.6% headline and 3.1% core.
Futures markets see a December rate hike as likely; the Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday with two dissents in favor of a hike.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 7 basis points to roughly 4.92% as investors fled to safety.
Tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil higher, with WTI crude trading above $100 a barrel.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: INTC (Intel): -29% — weak fourth-quarter guidance and a continuing PC slowdown; its worst day since 1974.
RDDT (Reddit): -29% — beat third-quarter results but gave a softer fourth-quarter revenue outlook.
REGN (Regeneron): about +12% by late morning — quarterly revenue jumped 36% to $5.1 billion.
TWLO (Twilio): about -17% — disappointing fourth-quarter organic growth forecast.
RBLX (Roblox): about -19% — forecast fourth-quarter bookings down 10% to 15%.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): about -12% in the afternoon — caught in the chip sell-off after Intel.
NVDA (Nvidia): -4.2% — chip sector selling.
CPRI (Capri): about +19% — raised its full-year forecast.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Exxon Mobil and Chevron beat estimates on strong refining margins and both hit record highs intraday.
Mondelez rose about 7% early after its results, and Regeneron was among the day's biggest large-cap gainers.
Amazon fell about 1.4% after its earnings miss and a large free cash flow outflow, even with AWS growing 39%.
Twilio and Stryker sank after reporting; Stryker was down about 10% early.
No major companies reported after Friday's close; the next big wave is Apple on Monday after the bell.

sections.title: Business News
items: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for about $17 billion in cash and stock, or $65 a share.
A $6.3 billion hack of the Binance crypto exchange weighed on bitcoin and crypto-linked stocks.
Sandisk beat earnings and announced an 8-for-1 stock split, but shares fell on worries memory prices have peaked.
Gold dropped more than 3% and fell back below $4,000 an ounce, while silver slid even more.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Next session is Monday, Nov. 2: S&P Global manufacturing PMI at 8:45 AM CT and ISM manufacturing PMI and construction spending at 9:00 AM CT.
Before the open: Marriott, Estee Lauder, Fox, Loews and IDEXX report.
After the close: Apple, Palantir, Vertex, ON Semiconductor and Roku report.
No Fed speakers are scheduled; the midterm elections are Tuesday and the October jobs report is Friday at 7:30 AM CT.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, October thirtieth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sinking low over the water, and friends, that last set of October was a gnarly one. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon guarding the cabana from seagulls. Say good evening to everybody, Gus! Here's the final set. The S and P five hundred fell one point eight percent to seven thousand five hundred seventy-nine. The Nasdaq dropped two point eight percent to twenty-five thousand four hundred forty-two. That was its worst day since early June. The Dow slipped about one percent to fifty-one thousand seven hundred eighty-six. The Russell two thousand lost two percent. Nearly seventy percent of stocks went down. Tech was the worst sector, off nearly five percent, and chip stocks took the biggest wipeout. The trigger was earnings that brought back worries about how much Big Tech is spending on artificial intelligence. For the month, the Nasdaq lost about five percent, while the Dow actually gained one and a half percent. Now the wind and weather. The employment cost index rose eight tenths of a percent last quarter. Two Fed officials, Alberto Musalem and Tom Barkin, said rates may need to go higher. Traders now see a December rate hike as likely. Bonds caught a safety bid, and the ten year Treasury yield fell about seven basis points to around four point nine two percent. Oil climbed after tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, with crude above one hundred dollars. Gold fell more than three percent and slipped back under four thousand dollars. Bitcoin lost more than two percent after a six billion dollar hack at the Binance exchange. The volatility index jumped about thirteen percent. Let's check the lineup. Intel plunged twenty-nine percent on weak guidance and a slow PC market. That was its worst day since nineteen seventy-four. Reddit also sank twenty-nine percent on a softer holiday outlook. Roblox fell about nineteen percent, Twilio about seventeen percent, and A M D about twelve percent. Nvidia gave back four percent. On the bright side, Regeneron surfed a monster swell, up about twelve percent by late morning after revenue jumped thirty-six percent. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Over on the tide chart, Exxon Mobil and Chevron beat estimates on strong refining profits and both touched record highs. Mondelez rallied after its report. Amazon slipped about one percent after an earnings miss, even with its cloud business growing thirty-nine percent. Beach talk now. DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for about seventeen billion dollars. And Sandisk announced an eight for one stock split, but the stock still fell. Tomorrow's forecast. The next session is Monday. The I S M manufacturing report lands at nine A M Central. Marriott and Estee Lauder report before the open, and Apple and Palantir report after the close. No Fed speakers are on deck. The midterm elections are Tuesday and the jobs report is Friday. So wax that board and stay a soul surfer through the chop. Catch the Dawn Patrol on Monday morning, and I'll be stoked to see you out there. Want me to call a wave for you? Type any stock, E T F or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
